change `ruvmymplmmoo` · [log `b64fabff131e`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/2324d402-3f17-421a-8a85-5b6846d2c728/b64fabff131e78eb11fe09363996d031287bc00b72222edcfe24b03d6b677f0c.jsonl.gz)

The cleanup loop's native stream, item N1, step 1. VF-010 says the own checker's branch probes are budgeted by wall-clock time (Engine::probe gives a probe as long as all the solver calls so far took, at least a second), so which side of a branch stays undecided, and with it the path order, depends on the machine: of 8 identical runs of Pricing#total's regression proof on cvm, 6 found the violation in about 4 s and 2 ran out of time. The new script lib/tests/reproducers/vf-010.sh compiles lib/tests/integration.rs's Pricing fixture and its rounding refactor, runs the entry's 'jvmcontract equivalence --target fixtures.Pricing#total --engine native --timeout 40' N times, prints each run's exit and the own checker's numbers, and exits 0 only when every run finds the violation. Tried once inline with a debug build: the violation in 2.7 s.

Verification pending: job 20261107-163057-vf-010-s-reproducer-before-the-fix-prici (verification/jobs/) runs it 8 times at this commit, before the fix, expecting exit 1. The fix comes next, and the same script at the fixing commit is VF-010's closing check, with the integration tests.
